title: Proposition NN: Keep and Spend Money for Education and Other Purposes

context.text: Placed on the ballot by the state legislature (legislatively referred statute). The Blue Book lists 14 statewide measures on the November 3, 2026 ballot.

question.text: Shall state investment in K-12 public education increase two percent each year for the next ten years, with investments used to increase teacher pay, improve teacher retention, lower class sizes, and increase access to career and technical courses, without raising taxes but instead funded by raising the annual limit on state fiscal year spending only by the amount spent on public K-12 education as a voter-approved revenue change, and requiring an annual publicly released, independent audit to show how the new investments are spent?

summary.text: Lets the state keep and spend revenue that TABOR would otherwise require to be refunded, up to a new limit equal to the current TABOR limit plus the highest amount previously spent on K-12 education from certain sources. Retained revenue first reimburses local governments for senior, disabled-veteran and Gold Star spouse property tax exemptions, then goes to a new Children's Account: K-12 teacher pay and retention, smaller classes and career and technical courses, and for ten years children's programs (prioritizing preschool and child care); afterward remaining money is for purposes set by the legislature. Fiscal impact per the Blue Book: TABOR refunds reduced by $329.9 million in 2026-27 and $521.0 million in 2027-28, which eliminates refunds in those years; state spending up by the same net amounts. Passes with a majority vote.

measure.yesMeans: Allows the state to keep some or all of the revenue that otherwise would be refunded to taxpayers under TABOR. The retained revenue must be spent on K-12 education, programs that support children, and any other purposes.
measure.noMeans: Maintains current TABOR refunds and funding levels for K-12 education, programs that support children, and other state purposes.

argumentsFor.text: Blue Book argument for: "Proposition NN raises teacher pay, reduces class sizes, and improves career and technical education, benefitting every school district in the state."
Blue Book argument for: "Proposition NN frees up funds that should already be supporting Colorado's children."

argumentsAgainst.text: Blue Book argument against: "Proposition NN is essentially a tax increase, permanently eliminating or reducing TABOR refunds."
Blue Book argument against: "Proposition NN eventually hands the state over $5 billion per year at the expense of Colorado families."

researchNotes: Source: the official 2026 Blue Book (Legislative Council Staff, nonpartisan), which gives the ballot title, the 'what your vote means' text, an analysis with arguments for and against, and the fiscal impact. Its 'for' and 'against' arguments are the staff's own summaries of the main arguments on each side, not statements from named campaigns; the booklet points to the Secretary of State's page for supporting and opposing organizations, which was not reviewed here. Ballotpedia is cited only for the certified-measure count. Ballotpedia notes a separate road-funding initiative was certified but withdrawn after its proponents reached an agreement with the state, so it is not on the ballot.
